outlooksByWeek.2: Puka Nacua managed to put up decent numbers despite the Rams' dismal offensive performance in their season opener, and he'll look to ramp up his production further in Week 2 against the Giants. Nacua recorded 74 of Matthew Stafford's 155 passing yards in Week 1 versus San Francisco, though he caught just five of nine targets. No other Rams pass catcher had more than three catches or 26 yards, so there's little doubt that Nacua unsurprisingly remains Stafford's favorite target. The Giants' defense looked good in a win over Dallas in Week 1, with top wideout CeeDee Lamb posting a modest 5-44-1 receiving line.

player.seasonOutlook: Nacua has defied the odds, emerging from fifth-round flier in 2023 to one of the most relied upon and productive offensive players in the league. Nacua has finished each of his three pro seasons sixth or better among receivers in fantasy PPG and peaked with a first-place finish last season. Matthew Stafford's top target led the league with 129 receptions and finished no lower than third among receivers in targets, yardage and touchdowns, while also adding 105 yards and one score as a rusher. More goal-line work would be nice (he has 11 end zone targets over the past two seasons), but Nacua's heavy usage in an elite offense locks in the 25-year-old as arguably the top receiver in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omarion Hampton looked like the clear lead back for the Chargers in their season-opening loss to the Cardinals, taking 12 carries for 43 yards and a touchdown, while backup Keaton Mitchell saw only four carries. Neither RB caught a pass as Justin Herbert had a very narrow target tree under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, connecting with just five different receivers. Hampton had been headed for a big rookie campaign before getting injured, so staying healthy will be the biggest factor in any potential 2026 breakout. He could post better numbers in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Hampton is primed for a breakout second season following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie campaign. The first-round pick was busy during nine appearances, averaging 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets. He scored five touchdowns, averaged 15.1 fantasy points per game (13th best) and ranked third among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF. With Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell as his primary competition, Hampton has a clear path to lead rusher duties in 2026, and his targets only figure to increase with Greg Roman out and Mike McDaniel in as the team's playcaller. Add in a much-improved offensive line with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back healthy, and Hampton has nothing short of elite upside. Value him as a fringe RB1 with room for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Nabers looked spry in his first game of the season for the Giants, a Week 1 victory over the Cowboys. Nabers led the G-Men in targets with nine, en route to six catches for 69 yards in the 28-20 triumph. Nabers showed no ill effects from his torn ACL and meniscus suffered in Week 4 last season, only needing to get tackled by his new head coach John Harbaugh to prove he could take a hit before suiting up. In Week 2, Nabers will face a Rams defense that struggled against the pass in Week 1, allowing 205 passing yards and three passing scores in its season opener. Nabers will likely be covered by all-pro cornerback Trent McDuffie, though.

player.seasonOutlook: Nabers is on the comeback trail after a torn ACL limited him to only four appearances last season. In 18 full games in his career, Nabers has a massive 35% target share (11.3 per game) and he's averaging 18.2 fantasy PPG. As a rookie, the 2024 sixth overall pick finished seventh or better among receivers in targets, receptions, yards and fantasy points despite missing two games and dealing with New York's offensive struggles. Nabers' massive target share allowed him a high floor, as he was a top-30 fantasy scorer in 13 of 15 games, including 10 straight to end the 2024 season. He essentially has a new quarterback (Jaxson Dart threw only three passes his way last season), a new coach (John Harbaugh), a new offensive playcaller (Matt Nagy) and is recovering from the knee, so there are a lot of variables here, but the 23-year-old still holds elite upside. A healthy Nabers should be valued as a mid-to-back-end WR1, but the potential for a slow start needs to be considered on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeVonta Smith was fairly quiet in the season opener for the Eagles. Smith finished with three catches for 53 yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. On the plus side, Smith led the team in targets for the game with six. The absence of A. J. Brown should pay dividends for Smith, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 215 passing yards and zero touchdowns through the air in its season opener, though the opposing quarterback was Geno Smith of the New York Jets. Expect Smith to become more involved against a suspect defense.

player.seasonOutlook: It's generally tough for a former Heisman Trophy winner and first-round draft pick to fly under the radar, but that has been the case for Smith in recent years. With all eyes on A.J. Brown, Smith has finished no lower than 30th among receivers in fantasy PPG in each of his five seasons (top 30 in PPG each of the last four). The "slim reaper" saw a big dip in touchdowns last season (four, after at least seven the prior three seasons), but remained very efficient (career 9.1 yards per target and 2.1 yards per route run). Smith has handled roughly one-quarter of the Eagles' targets throughout his career, and that may rise slightly after Brown was traded to New England. Smith, 27, is the Eagles' No. 1 receiver for the first time as a non-rookie and is well positioned for a strong WR2 campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: D'Andre Swift will aim to replicate a huge game as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Swift was dominant against the Panthers in Week 1, carrying the ball 18 times for 124 yards and three touchdowns. The veteran ball carrier topped any of his games in the 2025 season, showcasing that he should also benefit from a higher-scoring Chicago offense this year. He'll play a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but he has established himself more than the Packers' current RB room.

player.seasonOutlook: Swift is entering his seventh NFL season and third with Chicago. The veteran back was busy as both a rusher and receiver en route to clearing 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of his first two seasons with the Bears. Though he found the end zone 10 times and finished 17th among backs in fantasy points per game last season, Swift deferred substantial work to Kyle Monangai and is likely to be in even more of a timeshare in 2026. Still in his prime at age 27, Swift continues to play at a high level (4.87 yards per carry last season), but his role in the Chicago offense figures to limit him to low-ceiling RB2/flex production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Daniels overcame a slow start to nearly lead the Commanders to a comeback win against the Eagles in Week 1. Daniels finished the contest with 164 yards passing and two touchdowns, along with an additional 31 yards rushing for the game. Daniels will look to build some momentum in Week 2 versus an extremely suspect Dallas Cowboys defense. Dallas allowed the most yards in the NFL last season, and the supposedly revamped defense was trounced by the Giants in their 2026 opener. The Cowboys allowed 394 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns in an ugly 28-20 loss to Jaxson Dart and company.

player.seasonOutlook: Daniels is looking to bounce back after appearing in only seven games due to injury last season. The 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year began his career with a bang, tossing 25 touchdowns and adding 891 yards and six scores with his legs in his first season. He wasn't quite as dominant when healthy last season (16.3 points per game, compared to 20.9 in 2024), but he remained a major factor with his legs (58-278-2 in seven games, three of which were partial appearances). Daniels' supporting cast is underwhelming and he'll be working with a new playcaller (David Blough), but the dual-threat ability supplies the 25-year-old with elite upside. He's a strong QB1 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Sam LaPorta should remain a big part of Detroit's offense in Week 2 at Buffalo. In Week 1 against the Saints, LaPorta's 5-48-0 receiving line put him second to Amon-Ra St. Brown in receiving yards while tying Jahmyr Gibbs for second in catches. The fourth-year tight end will face a Bills defense that allowed 14.4 PPR points to Texans tight ends this past Sunday, so he'll have plenty of opportunities to build on his season-opening performance.

player.seasonOutlook: LaPorta has settled in as one of the league's top tight ends, but the 2023 second-round pick simply hasn't been able to match the fantasy success he enjoyed as a rookie. Since posting an 86-889-10 receiving line in 17 games that first season, LaPorta has totaled a 100-1,215-10 line in 25 games over the past two seasons. LaPorta's 2025 campaign was cut short by a back injury, otherwise he was well on his way to his third straight top-10 fantasy campaign (he finished seventh in PPG). The 25-year-old joins Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs as the clear "Core Four" targets in a good, pass-friendly Detroit offense, and is thus a solid fantasy TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathon Brooks is expected to operate as Carolina's No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Brooks received just four carries in the Week 1 loss, which is fewer than Chuba Hubbard (10) and AJ Dillon (five). However, all of Dillon's work came when the Panthers were down substantially in the fourth quarter. Brooks showed flashes of brilliance when on the field, most notably on a 48-yard catch and run. He could continue to take work from Hubbard as the season continues. However, he's in for a tough Week 2 matchup, with Atlanta allowing just 2.8 yards per rush attempt in Week 1, the best mark in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Brooks is hoping to get his career on track in 2026 after appearing in only one game since being drafted in the second round of the 2024 draft. Brooks spent most of his rookie season recovering from a torn ACL suffered while at the University of Texas. He returned in Week 12 and handled 12 touches in three games prior to retearing the same ACL and missing the entire 2025 season. Only 23 years old and skilled as a rusher and receiver, Brooks figures to eventually get his shot at a lead-back role in the pros. He's expected to battle for touches with Chuba Hubbard this season, so it's possible he quickly earns his way into a fantasy-relevant role. Consider him in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel for a Week 2 tilt against the Patriots. The former Indianapolis Colt secured all three targets for a team-high 58 yards in his debut for Pittsburgh. Pittman finished sixth in targets but still did plenty of damage with his opportunities, and if the Steelers want to throw the ball 40-plus times a game, he could develop into a reliable fantasy receiver. New England's defense ranks 21st in receiving yards allowed to WRs (161), but they will be playing at home with a rest advantage.

player.seasonOutlook: Pittman was traded to the Steelers after spending his first six NFL seasons with the Colts. The 2020 second-round pick handled a hefty 23.6% of Indianapolis' targets during his tenure, which helped him to four top-20 fantasy campaigns. Pittman has reached 800 receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while primarily operating as a short-to-intermediate target. The role has limited his scoring (he has 25 TDs in 95 games) and that may not change much with DK Metcalf on the other side in Pittsburgh. Of course, Pittman will be a featured target in an offense led by Aaron Rodgers. That's enough to put the 28-year-old squarely in the weekly WR3 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 2 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's now been placed on IR for the injury. The fifth-year running back (30 of 65 offensive snaps) and Aaron Jones (29 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps against the Packers, with Mason leading the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Unfortunately, Mason will now be out for at least the next four weeks, priming Jones for a bigger role moving forward.

player.seasonOutlook: Mason is back for his second season in Minnesota and will battle 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr. for backfield opportunities. Mason's role was almost exactly as expected last season, as he was utilized often as a rusher (9.9 carries per game), but a nonfactor as a receiver (1.0 targets per game). Mason reached 13 fantasy points just once in his 16 games and it was a 23.6-point effort in Week 3, one of five games Jones missed. Mason, 27, is an effective rusher -- his 5.10 YPC ranks third and his 2.42 YAC second among 54 RBs with 350-plus carries since he entered the league -- but adding so little as a receiver (34 career targets) severely limits his fantasy output. Even if Jones were to miss time, Mason would max out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Golden should remain a top look in Green Bay's passing offense in Week 2 against the Jets. Golden led the Packers in routes (40) and targets (12) in Week 1 against Minnesota, and he converted six catches for 95 yards. He already looks to have a big enough role for a second-year jump, and the pass-heavy nature of Green Bay's offense helps his case even more. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Golden is eyeing a Year 2 leap following a disappointing rookie season in which he was limited to 39 touches and failed to find the end zone in 14 regular-season games. Golden was limited to 53% of the snaps and never cleared six targets in a single outing. Some optimism was generated from Golden's 4-84-1 receiving line in the playoff loss to Chicago, but even with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks gone, it's unclear if he will actually see a big boost in usage in Matt LaFleur's offense considering that no Green Bay receiver has cleared a 21% target share since Davante Adams' departure prior to 2022. The speedy Golden, who also contributes as a rusher, is a recent first-round pick entering his second season. He's worth a speculative middle-round flier.

Tyson was selected by the Saints with the No. 8 overall pick of April's draft. He is a versatile receiver with decent size who led this rookie class with a 35% target share during the nine weeks he was active in 2025. Injuries cost him time during all four collegiate seasons, but he still managed a 158-2,282-22 receiving line in 33 games, posting a strong 2.73 YPRR along the way (third best in this class). Tyson suffered a hamstring injury in August and will miss a month or two of the regular season prior to taking over as the Saints' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave. Once healthy, Tyson has a path to a substantial role in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough and could find himself on the WR3 radar. Of course, with the injury, he's only worth a late flier.

The defending Super Bowl champions, who benefited greatly from what was the league's top-scoring fantasy defense, draw one of the toughest overall schedules as a ?reward.? Only the Cardinals (Weeks 2 and 9), Raiders (Week 10) and Giants (Week 14) appear to be clear plus matchups, and the team must also deal with the offseason losses of S Coby Bryant, edge rusher Boye Mafe and CB Riq Woolen. Mike Macdonald might extract maximum effort from his defenses, but some regression should be expected with this unit.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Kincaid will look to match a career outing when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Kincaid had a personal-best 130 yards in his season debut but, more importantly, played 77% of the team's snaps after topping 50% just three times last year. If Kincaid remains on the field at this rate, he's likely to soar past his previous season's output. He'll face a defense on Thursday night that allowed 87 yards and two touchdowns to tight ends in Week 1, suggesting his statistical surge can continue.

player.seasonOutlook: Kincaid is perhaps fantasy's biggest wild card among tight ends. The 2023 first-round pick has occasionally flashed a high ceiling (he actually led qualified tight ends in YPT and YPRR last season), but he also has missed substantial action (nine games the past two years) and has disappeared way too often (he failed to clear 13.1 fantasy points in any game in 2024, and never cleared six targets in a game in 2025). Kincaid was limited to a 37% snap share when active last season, and he has yet to finish a season better than 14th in fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old has TE1 upside, but he's tough to trust and has added target competition (WR DJ Moore) in 2026. Consider Kincaid only in the mid-to-late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Evan McPherson will look to stay perfect when the Bengals visit the Texans in Week 2. He nailed all four of his field-goal attempts, including kicks of 55 and 58 yards, and made all three PATs during Cincinnati's 33-27 win in the season opener. McPherson should remain a top fantasy kicker as a member of one of the NFL's elite offenses. Houston gave up 36 points and 409 total yards in their Week 1 loss to the Bills.

Emmett Johnson contributed in his NFL debut, gaining 24 yards on eight carries and catching both his targets for 44 yards in a season-opening win over the Broncos. Kansas City leaned heavily on its ground game, with Kenneth Walker having a career-best day on 26 touches. Johnson's volume may be repeatable if this proves to be the team's offensive formula in 2026 and they continue building big second-half leads. Johnson will look to take advantage of his opportunities in Week 2 against a Colts defense that was just steamrolled by Derrick Henry but ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs last season.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was selected by the Chiefs in the fifth round of April's draft. His career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is fourth best in this RB rookie class and his elusiveness helped him to 1,451 rushing yards (fourth in the nation and first in this class) last season. His lack of speed -- last among 10 RBs who ran the 40-yard dash (4.56) and speed score (93) at the combine -- and size limits him after initial contact (career 2.86 YAC), but he can help out in the passing game (92 collegiate receptions). Johnson and Brashard Smith are set to handle No. 2/3 duties behind Kenneth Walker III. Smith will be worth rostering only if Walker misses action.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keaton Mitchell couldn't capitalize on his preseason buzz in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals. He got only four carries, turning them into a mere nine yards, and failed to see a target. The former Raven is the clear backup to Omarion Hampton in the backfield, but Mitchell may need much more favorable game scripts to get meaningful volume. He'll try to contribute in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell signed with the Chargers after spending his first three NFL seasons with Baltimore. The 2023 UDFA will compete with Kimani Vidal for change-of-pace touches behind starter Omarion Hampton. Mitchell has been limited to 140 touches over his first three NFL seasons, but he has been extremely productive when called upon. His career 6.34 yards per carry ranks second and his 2.50 YAC fourth among 89 backs with 100-plus carries since 2023. He has also put up 184 yards on 23 targets (8.0 YPT). Mitchell is on the small side, so his ceiling is likely capped (he has never cleared 11 touches in a game), but the 24-year-old would be worth adding should Hampton miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: James Cook will seek higher volume when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Cook logged just 13 carries in a surprisingly high-scoring opener in Houston, going for 57 yards while adding three catches on four targets but failing to reach the end zone after scoring 32 times over the last two seasons. Detroit's defense allowed a fair 4.0 yards per carry last week but is far more vulnerable through the air. Cook's bulk role is unquestioned, keeping his floor stable while a potential shootout creates more chances for him to reach pay dirt.

player.seasonOutlook: Cook signed a contract extension last offseason and was immediately vaulted into the biggest role of his career. The 2022 second-round NFL draft pick finished in the top five among backs in carries, rushing yards (league-high 1,621), touchdowns and yards per carry (5.25). The one limiting factor in Cook's fantasy output was a minimal receiving role (his 40 targets ranked 26th among RBs), but he still came through with a sixth-place finish in fantasy points. The 26-year-old is set to play the same role in Joe Brady's scheme and will be a candidate for his third straight double-digit touchdown campaign as long as Josh Allen is under center. Consider Cook a midrange RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Walker earned his big salary in his Kansas City debut, rumbling for a career-high 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries while catching three of six targets for 18 yards and another score in a season-opening win over the Broncos. It was the kind of volume Walker rarely garnered in Seattle, but the fifth-year RB is being counted on to handle bell-cow duties with his new team, as rookie Emmett Johnson figures to be his primary backup for most or all of the season. Walker will aim to keep rolling in Week 2 against a Colts defense that just got steamrolled by Derrick Henry, but which ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.

player.seasonOutlook: Walker signed with the Chiefs after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Seahawks. The reigning Super Bowl MVP and PFF's highest-graded running back from 2025, Walker is poised for feature-back duties in a good, Andy Reid-led offense. Having worked in a committee most of last season, Walker was limited to only five touchdowns and 11.3 fantasy points per game (both career lows), but he still generated 252 touches and a career-high 1,309 yards. He has yet to finish a season better than 18th in fantasy points (12th on a per-game basis) and has missed at least two games in three of four seasons in the league, but the 25-year-old's ability to contribute at a high level as a rusher and receiver is enough to position him as, at least, a fringe RB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Pickens was held to just 28 yards in the season opener for the Cowboys. Pickens did finish second on the team in targets with six, but was rather quiet still by his standards. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Pickens with an uninspiring output in Week 1. Pickens will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.

player.seasonOutlook: Pickens drew the franchise tag from Dallas after a career year in which he ranked near the top of the wide receiver position in most categories, including catches, yards, TDs, end zone targets (second with 18) and air yards (fourth with 1,576). Fantasy's No. 5-scoring receiver in 2025 certainly benefited from CeeDee Lamb missing time (24% target share, or 8.8 per game, and 24.2 fantasy PPG in four games Lamb was injured), but his "with Lamb" splits were also strong. Consider: In 12 full games with Lamb, Pickens handled a 23% target share (8.3 per game) and averaged 16.1 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth at the position over the full season. The 25-year-old will play the same role in Dallas' high-scoring offense in 2026 and has the look of a strong fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Garrett Wilson should maintain steady volume for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. He garnered seven targets in a run-heavy situation to open the year, catching six for 79 yards. Green Bay's secondary is suspect and just allowed Vikings' top receiver Justin Jefferson to score twice, despite Carson Wentz being under center. The Jets will likely need to throw more in Week 2, potentially pushing Wilson into double-digit targets and setting him up for elevated numbers.

player.seasonOutlook: Wilson is eyeing a bounce-back following an injury-shortened 2025 that limited him to seven games. It was the first time Wilson had missed time, having appeared in all 51 games during his first three seasons. The 2022 first-round pick ranked no lower than sixth among receivers in targets in each of those years, but he failed to produce a fantasy campaign better than 20th (PPG) due to New York's quarterback woes. Wilson was off to a hot start last season (four TDs, 14.2 fantasy PPG) thanks to a massive 33% target share (second highest). New York's signal-caller problems still aren't completely solved, but veteran Geno Smith should provide an upgrade over last year's Justin Fields/Tyrod Taylor duo. Wilson, 26, is one of the best raw talents at the position and should be valued as a good WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tee Higgins and the Bengals visit the Texans for a Week 2 battle between two playoff hopefuls. He caught three of six targets for 59 yards during Cincinnati's season-opening victory. Higgins tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing behind Mike Gesicki for the lead in receiving yards. He draws a favorable matchup against Houston's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Higgins may be overshadowed by teammate Ja'Marr Chase, but that hasn't stopped the veteran receiver from playing a key role near the goal line in the Bengals' pass-friendly offense. Despite missing seven games over the past two seasons, Higgins sits eighth among receivers in end zone targets (24) and fourth in touchdowns (21) during the span. The 2020 second-round pick finished both seasons in the top 20 in fantasy points (overall and per game). Durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2020) and a limited target share are concerns here, but Higgins' combination of talent and role in a Joe Burrow-led offense are enough to allow fringe-WR2 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Joe Burrow and the Bengals travel to take on the Texans in Week 2. Burrow completed 25 of 35 passes for 254 yards with one TD and one INT, and he rushed five times for 20 yards in their season-opening win. Houston ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (39.0) to QBs after Josh Allen torched them for 357 scrimmage yards and four TDs. Burrow will look to get Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins more involved after the receivers combined for 71 yards on just five catches.

player.seasonOutlook: Burrow will attempt to bounce back after injuries limited him to eight games in 2025. The 29-year-old has now missed at least six games in three of his six pro seasons, including two of his past three. Burrow was still a starting-caliber fantasy quarterback when active last season (top-12 scorer in five of his final six games), but his ceiling was limited by a near complete lack of rushing (41 yards on 14 carries). Burrow was a top-five scoring quarterback in each of his past two full seasons, and coach Zac Taylor cut back a bit on his extreme pass-heavy playcalling last season, so Burrow is best valued as more of a midrange QB1 than an elite option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tucker Kraft should continue to have a big role in Green Bay's offense as they face the Jets in Week 2. Kraft reeled in three of six targets for 65 yards against the Vikings in Week 1, but he was definitely a huge focus of their defensive scheme. The star tight end will luckily face a New York defense that should be less menacing this Sunday, as they ceded a lower-half 15.4 PPR points per game to tight ends in the 2025 campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Kraft's steady career progression had him on the cusp of a full-on breakout last season, but all was derailed by a torn ACL in Week 9. Prior to the injury, Kraft had seen 10 targets in consecutive games, one of which included a career-high 33.3 fantasy points. Through Week 8, only Jake Ferguson had more fantasy points. Granted, Kraft took advantage of a super easy schedule and was way over his head in the TD department (six TDs with an expected total of 1.8 and only two end zone targets), but his boost in usage and terrific RAC skills (he has led the position in the category each of his three seasons) were enough to get him into the weekly TE1 mix. Kraft's recovery will need to be monitored, but even if he's ready for Week 1, a dip in production is possible in his first year back from the major injury. He's a risky middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: J.K. Dobbins wasn't a big part of the Broncos' game plan in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, as the veteran running back had only eight carries for 36 yards. RJ Harvey's volume was similar, with seven touches to Dobbins' eight, but turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Dobbins averaged over 80 scrimmage yards last season in the 10 regular-season games he was healthy, so better days should be ahead for Denver's lead back, although they may not come right away. In Week 2, he'll face a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.

player.seasonOutlook: Dobbins re-signed with Denver and will attempt to fend off sophomore RJ Harvey for the team's lead-back job. With both active during Weeks 1-10 last season (10 games), Dobbins handled 153 carries (60% team share) and 15 targets (4%), compared to 50 carries (20%) and 29 targets (9%) for Harvey. Dobbins ran well (5.05 yards per carry) when healthy, but he was limited to four touchdowns and was a nonfactor as a receiver (37 yards on 15 targets) en route to averaging 11.6 fantasy points (27th). Dobbins enters his age-27 campaign having yet to play a full season in his career (seven-plus missed games in four of the past five years) and without much value even when active (he has never produced a top-20 fantasy campaign). Dobbins is an underwhelming flex option with added value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Downs is hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league flex for the Colts' Week 2 trip to Kansas City. His four targets in the Week 1 loss to Baltimore tied for fourth on the team with Jonathan Taylor, as Daniel Jones threw more frequently to Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen and Tyler Warren. In 17 appearances since the start of last season, Downs is averaging a pedestrian 35.5 receiving yards per game in the Colts' run-heavy offense.

player.seasonOutlook: Downs has settled in as a serviceable slot receiver, which has helped him to finish in the 35-to-45 range among WRs in total fantasy points in each of his three NFL seasons. Downs peaked with a 72-803-5 receiving line in 2024, but took a step back in a crowded offense last season, and failed to deliver a single fantasy week better than 15th at the position. The undersized Downs isn't an option near the goal line, as he hasn't cleared five touchdowns or three end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old has a path to a slightly larger role in 2026 with Michael Pittman Jr. gone, leaving Alec Pierce, Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen as his primary target competition. Downs is a sleeper for flex production in PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Zhaun Stribling isn't likely to play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup versus Miami. Stribling suffered an ankle injury during his NFL debut last Thursday against the Rams and is expected to miss at least a month of action. While he's out, Demarcus Robinson is slated to take on the 49ers' No. 3 wideout role.

player.seasonOutlook: Stribling was selected by the 49ers with the 33rd overall pick in April's draft. Stribling had a productive collegiate run, catching 44-plus passes in four of his five seasons, three of which came with different schools. That production included 52-882-6 and 55-811-6 receiving lines at Oklahoma State and Ole Miss over the past two seasons. Stribling primarily worked as a perimeter receiver and peaked with a 22% target share with OSU in 2024. His overall efficiency is pedestrian, but he has good size and speed (4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) and is a plus blocker. Stribling has plenty competition for Year 1 targets (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey), so a slow start is possible, but it's likely he'll eventually find his way to a bigger role and fantasy relevance. He's a fine mid-round upside pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes in the first 33 minutes of Jacksonville's lopsided Week 1 win over the Browns before the Jaguars took their foot off the gas. He has 22 touchdown passes in his last eight starts, but the surging QB could face a stiffer test in a Week 2 road game against the Broncos. They boasted the NFL's third-stingiest scoring defense last season but just gave up 31 points to the Chiefs in Week 1. Lawrence has been effective enough recently to warrant starting in fantasy despite the daunting matchup, but he's unlikely to give managers a top-five performance in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Lawrence is entering his sixth NFL season after a breakout 2025 in which he ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in pass attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns, as well as top 10 in carries, yards and TDs. He reeled off seven consecutive top-10 fantasy outings to finish the season. Lawrence's efficiency has been fine, at best, but he continues to generate big volume, having finished in the top 10 among QBs in pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. With a strong, deep group of pass catchers and Liam Coen back as playcaller, the 26-year-old is well positioned for mid-to-back-end QB1 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Blake Corum was one of few Rams players to have a good game on offense in their season-opening loss, and he'll look for more success in Week 2 against the Giants. Corum led Los Angeles with 54 rushing yards on just 10 carries versus San Francisco last Thursday, averaging 5.4 YPC after putting up an average of 5.1 YPC during the regular season last year. Kyren Williams remains the Rams' lead back, but there's little doubt that Corum has forced his way into a substantial role as well. The Giants held Dallas' No. 1 RB Javonte Williams to 3.4 YPC on 12 totes in Week 1, though Williams did score a rushing TD and put up a 5-31-1 line through the air.

player.seasonOutlook: Corum has spent his first two NFL seasons as Kyren Williams' backup, and that's expected to be the case again in 2026. The 2024 third-round NFL draft pick played well in the role last season, averaging a healthy 5.1 yards per carry (seventh among RBs) and scoring six touchdowns on 145 carries. However, Corum played only 29% of the Rams' snaps and remained a nonfactor as a receiver (36 yards on 14 targets). The 25-year-old has no standalone fantasy value, but he's an elite insurance stash, as he'd launch into the fringe-RB1 mix in the Rams' high-powered offense should Williams miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Reed will look to make more of his opportunities as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Reed struggled even with seven targets in a loss to the Vikings, logging just three catches for 20 yards. The fourth-year playmaker could start to slip into a WR3 role if he continues to play similarly, but luckily there appears to be plenty of targets to go around in the short term. Reed will face a New York defense that ranked middle-of-the-pack against wide receivers this past Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: Reed began his NFL career with a pair of top-30 fantasy campaigns, but the Green Bay slot receiver was limited to only seven appearances last season due to injury. Even when active, Reed wasn't as effective as in years past, averaging 6.9 fantasy PPG and finding the end zone once (Week 1). This comes after the 2023 second-round pick produced 75 touches, 900-plus yards and seven-plus touchdowns in each of his first two seasons. The 26-year-old signed a contract extension in April and will battle the likes of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Savion Williams for targets this season. While he'll likely hit for the occasional solid game, his limited usage (career-high 18% target share) will put a cap on his fantasy upside. He's barely in the flex conversation in PPR leagues.

Though the 2025 Eagles took a step backwards from the defensive stalwart that won Super Bowl LIX, their D/ST scored only 12 fewer total fantasy points and finished eighth at the position in scoring. Coordinator Vic Fangio typically extracts the most from his defenses, but the departures of S Reed Blankenship, LB Nakobe Dean, DE Brandon Graham and LB Jaelen Phillips heighten the challenge -- though the additions of LB Jonathan Greenard and CB Riq Woolen at least soften the blow. At least the team starts off with some soft matchups (WSH, Week 1; @TEN, Week 2), but be prepared to swap quickly if they're underperforming.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Loop and the Ravens look to keep rolling at home versus the Saints in Week 2. Baltimore put up 41 points in their Week 1 victory, and Loop was a perfect 7-for-7 on his attempts. He made all five PATs and drilled both field-goal attempts-one from 57 yards out and one from 45. As long as he's the starting kicker, Loop should see plenty of scoring chances in this high-scoring Ravens offense. He'll try to stay perfect against a New Orleans defense that gave up 31 points to the Lions in the season opener.

Adonai Mitchell will look to stretch the field for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Mitchell hauled in all three of his targets to open the year, finishing with 60 yards. Green Bay allowed a mere 7.7 yards per target in Week 1, but that was largely due to facing Carson Wentz for the bulk of the game. Their secondary remains vulnerable and will likely commit multiple bodies to Garrett Wilson, setting up Mitchell for a few plays downfield in single coverage. Mitchell seems likely to continue his low-volume, high-upside role in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell is entering his first full campaign with the Jets, having been acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade during the 2025 season. After playing sparingly during his first 25 NFL games (all with the Colts), the 2024 second-round pick handled a hefty 24.4% target share in eight games with New York last season. The usage led to two fantasy outings with 17-plus points, but he was otherwise a nonfactor (4.0 PPG). Efficiency remains an issue, as Mitchell's 44% catch rate ranks last, and his 6.0 yards per target is fourth worst among 77 receivers with 100-plus targets since he entered the league. The vertical threat will compete with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. for No. 2 duties opposite a now-healthy Garrett Wilson in the Jets' Geno Smith-led offense. Mitchell, 23, is not worth much more than late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathan Taylor carried the Colts' offense with 121 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 22 touches in the season opener. His heavy Week 1 workload was encouraging considering the Colts trailed by 18 points at halftime and lost by that same margin to the Ravens. Indianapolis could face another negative game script in Week 2 at Kansas City, but Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1, even with the team around him looking shaky. Taylor led the NFL with 323 carries and 18 rushing TDs last season while compiling 1,963 scrimmage yards.

player.seasonOutlook: Taylor enters the 2026 season having improved in fantasy points per game in each of the past three years. Last season, he delivered his best production since his huge 2021 campaign, as he paced the NFL in carries and TDs while finishing second in carries inside the 5-yard line (19) and fourth in fantasy points. A piece of the step forward was increased usage in the passing game, as he ranked in the top 10 among backs in routes, targets, catches and receiving yards, setting career highs in each. Taylor's season likely would've been even better had QB Daniel Jones not been injured, as the running back averaged 24.8 points with Jones but 12.9 without him. Jones is expected to be ready to play in Week 1, so the 27-year-old Taylor is safe to value as a mid- to high-end RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trey McBride marches into a Week 2 matchup versus Seattle fresh off a strong season-opening performance in Arizona's victory against the Chargers. McBride led Cardinals pass catchers across the board with nine catches, 13 targets and 95 yards in that win, and he scored the team's lone passing touchdown. The All-Pro is essentially matchup-proof as possibly the league's premier tight end, though he'll draw a tough Seahawks defense in Week 2. However, it's worth noting that Seattle gave up the sixth-most receiving yards to tight ends during the regular season last year.

player.seasonOutlook: McBride has emerged as one of the league's top pass catchers -- not just tight ends -- as he trails only Ja'Marr Chase in targets (317) and receptions (252) over the past two seasons and is sixth in receiving yards (2,385). McBride led the tight end position in every fantasy-relevant counting stat in 2025, and his league-high 15 top-12 fantasy weeks were six more than any other player at the position. He finished third in the NFL with 17 end zone targets. McBride really thrived when Jacoby Brissett (21.1 PPG) replaced Kyler Murray (12.5) under center, which only adds to his 2026 appeal. The 26-year-old should be on your radar at the first-/second-round turn.

outlooksByWeek.2: Javonte Williams scored twice in the season opener for Dallas. Williams rushed for 41 yards and a touchdown, while catching five passes for 31 yards and a second score, though the Cowboys fell to the Giants by a score of 28-20. Nevertheless, Williams appears to have picked up right where he left off in 2025 during his career year. In Week 2, Williams will face a Washington defense that was gutted on the ground in its season opener. The Commanders yielded 136 yards on the ground, which places them 26th in the NFL in that category currently.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams re-signed with the Cowboys following a successful first year with the team. After failing to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign during his final three seasons in Denver, Williams finished 12th in 2025, setting career-best marks in carries, rushing yards, touches (287), scrimmage yards (1,338) and yards per carry (4.77). He also scored a career-high 13 touchdowns after totaling 16 during his first four campaigns, and his 16 carries inside the 5-yard line were fifth most among backs. That helped offset his receiving struggles, as his 2.7 yards per target was last among qualified RBs. With minimal competition for touches in a high-scoring Dallas offense, the 26-year-old is a solid RB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ladd McConkey seemed headed for a big performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching five of seven targets for 81 yards and a touchdown. However, he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter after a big hit left him with a rib injury. McConkey still led the team in receiving yards and was on the receiving end of Justin Herbert's only TD pass, and the club doesn't seem to believe the injury is serious. His status for Week 2 will remain up in the air until later in the week, if not right up to kickoff. If he is able to suit up, McConkey will be facing a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points per game allowed to WRs last season.

player.seasonOutlook: McConkey is looking to rebound after falling short of high expectations in 2025. The 2024 second-round pick was terrific as a rookie (82-1,155-7 receiving line and a 12th-place finish among WRs in fantasy points), but dipped to 66-789-6 line and a 30th-place finish last season. Though he ran considerably more routes, saw similar target numbers and was used a lot more near the goal line (seventh among WRs with 12 end zone targets), McConkey's efficiency plummeted, with his catch rate dipping from 74% to 62% and his yards per target from 10.4 to 7.4. The good news is that there's reason for optimism that he'll bounce back, as he has a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel, the Chargers' offense figures to improve with a much healthier line, and Keenan Allen is out of the picture. McConkey, 24, makes for a fine fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Etienne is expected to remain New Orleans' top running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Despite Alvin Kamara (knee) being sidelined for the Week 1 overtime loss, Etienne only received nine carries, tying Kendre Miller for the most on the team. However, Etienne was busy as a receiver, catching seven of nine targets for 46 yards, which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. He could be in for another productive week, as Baltimore's defense allowed 28.1 PPR fantasy points to running backs in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Etienne signed with the Saints after spending the first five seasons of his pro career with the Jaguars. The 2021 first-round pick has produced at least 1,399 scrimmage yards in three of the past four seasons and scored a career-high 13 touchdowns in 2025. A capable rusher and receiver, Etienne has already reached 1,000-plus rushing yards three times and has 35-plus catches in each of the past four seasons. Even if the Saints retain Alvin Kamara as a situational player, Etienne will have a clear path to feature-back duties in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough. That will be enough to position the 27-year-old for his third top-15 fantasy campaign in four years. Consider Etienne a solid RB2 target with backend RB1 upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rome Odunze will seek to do more as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Odunze was unable to capitalize on the highest-scoring Week 1 game ever, as he finished the game with two catches for 52 yards. The third-year receiver still figures to be a top target for Caleb Williams moving forward, especially in closer matchups where a consistent option is needed. Odunze will face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points to WRs (55.2) in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Odunze opened the 2025 season with a bang, scoring five touchdowns in his first four games and producing 15-plus fantasy points in each game. Things fell apart from there, as the 2024 first-round pick went on to deliver one touchdown and two double-digit fantasy outings over his next eight games prior to missing Weeks 14 through 18 due to injury. On the plus side, Odunze remained heavily targeted throughout the season, especially near the goal line, and he is ninth in the NFL with 24 end zone targets since he was drafted. On the other hand, his connection with Caleb Williams needs work, as his 48% catch rate ranked near the basement at the position. Odunze, 24, is still ascending and has a clearer path to targets with DJ Moore out of the mix. He's a candidate for a Year 3 leap and should be valued as a WR3 with upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Hurts tossed three touchdowns in Week 1 for the Eagles. Hurts was not terribly efficient, though did hit on several big plays en route to the 24-22 win. Hurts also rushed for 46 yards in a brand new offense under the direction of offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. In Week 2, Philadelphia will face a dismal Titans squad that allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurts enters his seventh NFL season and sixth as the starter in Philadelphia. The 28-year-old tossed a career-high 25 touchdowns last season, but his rushing production was way down (105-421-8 after delivering at least 139 carries, 605 yards and 10 TDs in each of the prior four seasons). Hurts' fantasy production dipped, as his 18.7 points per game was his lowest as a starter and ranked eighth at the position after three straight top-five campaigns. Hurts' supporting cast remains strong (even without A.J. Brown), and new playcaller Sean Mannion very well could add some juice back to the offense. Hurts' fantasy stock is down a bit from years past, but his dual-threat ability locks him in as a midrange QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Evans had a strong 49ers debut last Thursday versus the Rams and will next face Miami in Week 2. Evans caught six passes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the season opener, with his score coming on a two-yard connection with quarterback Brock Purdy. The veteran wideout tied with Deebo Samuel for the most targets among SF wideouts, so he looks to have already established a good rapport with Purdy. Evans could be in for another strong performance Sunday against a Titans defense that allowed three passing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.

player.seasonOutlook: Evans signed with the 49ers after spending his first 12 NFL seasons with the Buccaneers. The future Hall of Famer famously opened his career with 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, but that streak ended when he missed nine games due to injury last season. Even when active, Evans wasn't his usual, productive self, delivering only one weekly fantasy finish better than 23rd and none better than 11th. Now 33 years old, Evans is past his prime, but he's in line for a decent chunk of the targets, especially near the goal line, in Kyle Shanahan's high-scoring offense. Evans is best valued as a touchdown-dependent WR3/flex with more value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots. He rushed eight times for 15 yards and caught two of five targets for another six yards during Pittsburgh's Week 1 20-13 win over Atlanta. Dowdle's backfield partner, Jaylen Warren, was much more efficient with his 15 touches, which he turned into 73 scrimmage yards. It will be difficult to trust Dowdle in a tilt versus New England's 14th-ranked defense, which has allowed 84 rushing yards to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alec Pierce led the Colts with 61 receiving yards in the season opener despite battling a heel injury heading into the game. In addition, he left during the first half to get X-rays on his hand and wrist after hitting a defender's helmet. His practice participation is likely to be affected by those injuries, but Pierce is seemingly on track to suit up in Week 2 against the Chiefs and can be viewed as a solid WR3 or flex option. He brings big-play ability to an otherwise underwhelming Colts passing game, averaging at least 21.3 yards per catch in each of the past two seasons and leading the team with 1,003 receiving yards in 2025.

player.seasonOutlook: Pierce has spent the majority of his first four NFL seasons as a situational deep threat, but that didn't stop him from becoming one of the league's highest-paid wide receivers during the offseason. The 2022 second-round pick is fresh off a career year and he's now paced all receivers in YPR, YPT and aDOT each of the last two seasons. However, he's yet to finish a season better than 48th at WR in target share (18%), 42nd in targets (84), 45th in catches (47), 18th in yards (1,003), 18th in TDs (seven) or 25th in fantasy PPG. Of course, with Michael Pittman Jr. no longer in the mix, Pierce is a good bet for a more well-rounded role as Daniel Jones' top target. There's some risk here, but the 26-year-old's hefty contract suggests we should take him seriously as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jakobi Meyers maintains a high floor, though he's a low-ceiling fantasy WR3 or flex play for Jacksonville's Week 2 home game against Denver's elite defense. Meyers has posted at least 39 receiving yards in all 10 of his games with the Jaguars since coming over in a midseason trade last year, including 40 receiving yards and a TD in the Week 1 win over Cleveland. Parker Washington and Brian Thomas have more downfield playmaking capability, but Meyers should see his share of short targets with Trevor Lawrence likely looking to get the ball out quickly to counter a Broncos pass rush that led the league with 68 sacks last season.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the league's most underrated players, Meyers is entering his first full season with Jacksonville after being acquired via trade in November. The 2019 UDFA has produced 800-plus receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while operating primarily as a short-to-intermediate target. More of a solid producer than a high-ceiling contributor, Meyers has finished no lower than 32nd in fantasy points over the last five seasons, but has yet to do better than 19th. The 29-year-old isn't much of a touchdown scorer (23 TDs in 78 games since 2021) and has substantial target competition via Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Brenton Strange and Travis Hunter. Meyers is a good player, but is likely to cap out as a flex option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Addison will look to record his first reception of the year as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Addison ran the second-most routes for Minnesota in Week 1 against the Packers, but he was unable to convert on either of his two targets. Veteran quarterback Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion), relied more on tight ends T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver behind Justin Jefferson. This could make Addison's role remains small as long as Wentz remains under center. With that being said, the Bears' defense did allow the fourth-most PPR points to wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1, which could open up Minnesota's passing game.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing with a 70-911-10 receiving line on 108 targets as a rookie in 2023, Addison has seen his target, reception, yardage and touchdown totals decrease each of the last two seasons. A few missed games were partially to blame for the dips, but Minnesota's quarterback woes were the main culprit in 2025, as Addison went from 10 TDs and a 65% catch rate in both 2023 and 2024 to three TDs and a 53% catch rate last season. Addison already has a pair of top-25 fantasy campaigns to his name, but it may be a stretch for him to get there in 2026 with Kyler Murray leading the Minnesota offense, not to mention Jauan Jennings' addition to the lineup. The 24-year-old is best valued as WR4/flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harrison Mevis is coming off a quiet season opener as the Rams prepare to face the Giants in Week 2. Los Angeles' offense was held by the 49ers to just seven points last Thursday, and Mevis didn't get the opportunity to attempt any field goals. The Rams figure to be much more prolific on that side of the ball most weeks, so Mevis should be more active moving forward, though last year he attempted 39 PATs to just 13 field goals. The Giants' defense put up a good performance in a Week 1 win over Dallas, with star kicker Brandon Aubrey getting no field-goal tries.

Khalil Shakir will look to remain Josh Allen's security blanket in Week 2 when the Bills host the Lions. Shakir managed four grabs on six targets to open the season, finishing with 50 yards. He operated underneath while newly acquired DJ Moore stretched the field. The Lions' vulnerable secondary gave up 410 yards passing in Week 1, but Shakir will likely be limited by shorter routes, creating a safe but uninspiring fantasy option.

player.seasonOutlook: Shakir has settled in as a reliable, short-range target for Josh Allen, though the role hasn't led to much fantasy success. The 2022 fifth-round pick has cleared a 20% target share and 70 catches in consecutive seasons, ranking top five among receivers in catch rate and RAC both years. A nonfactor near the goal line, however, Shakir totaled eight TDs and five end zone targets during the span. Shakir finished the two seasons just outside of the top 35 fantasy receivers and will now have to compete with DJ Moore for the team lead in targets. Shakir was already barely worth flex consideration, so the potential for a slight decrease in target volume suggests the 26-year-old is no more than a low-ceiling bench option.

No team has as soft a schedule on the defensive side of things than do the Ravens; only the Cowboys (Week 3), Bengals (7 and 17) and Bills (8) stand out as particularly challenging matchups. That's a good thing, considering this unit finished a disappointing 21st in scoring last season. The Ravens still have stars on the defensive side, and the change in head coach to Jesse Minter and defensive coordinator to Anthony Weaver should fuel a rebound to some degree.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Von Achane should again be featured for the Dolphins against the 49ers in Week 2. Achane recorded only 11 carries to open the year, with Miami falling behind early-something that is likely to be a weekly occurrence-but he logged five targets. In Week 1, San Francisco allowed 114 rushing yards and a touchdown plus four receptions to backs, and with Achane rarely leaving the field (88% snap share), the makings are there for a safe outing with scoring upside.

player.seasonOutlook: Achane has quickly staked his claim as one of the best running backs in the league. The 2023 third-round pick has scored either 11 or 12 touchdowns in each of his three seasons and put up a career-high 1,838 scrimmage yards in 2025. Achane's elite receiving production is nothing new (he has finished in the top five among backs in targets and receiving yards in each of the past two years), but he made another leap forward as a rusher last season, finishing fifth at the position in rushing yards. His 5.62 yards per carry is best among qualified backs since he entered the league. The 24-year-old is eyeing his third straight top-five fantasy campaign, and while that might be tricky in an overhauled Miami offense led by quarterback Malik Willis, Achane has minimal competition for touches and should easily be the offensive centerpiece. He's a solid RB1 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Houston for a Week 2 showdown versus the Texans. He rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a TD and brought in five of six targets for another 22 yards during Cincinnati's Week 1 victory over Tampa Bay. Brown is the clear-cut lead back on a high-powered offense, and he should continue to see a hefty workload on the ground and in the passing game. However, Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, so consider this a less-than-favorable matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown is entering his fourth NFL season and third as Cincinnati's lead back. His 2025 season got off to a rocky start (10.1 fantasy points per game and one touchdown during his first seven games), but it turned around drastically down the stretch (21.2 points per game and 10 TDs during his final 10 games). The improvement coincided with Cincinnati's improved QB play, which should continue into 2026 with a healthy Joe Burrow. Brown has yet to finish a season higher than 16th in carries or rushing yards, but he has scored exactly 11 TDs and has finished fifth in receptions in each of the past two years, both of which have resulted in top-10 fantasy campaigns. The 26-year-old once again has minimal competition for touches in a very good Bengals offense. He's best valued as a fringe RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top wideout in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Olave definitely benefitted from Tyler Shough's 56 pass attempts during the Week 1 overtime loss. However, New Orleans averaged 34.8 pass attempts per game in 2025, so Olave will likely continue to see loads of volume. Additionally, he saw a 25 percent target share, which should remain steady until Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) returns later this season. Olave is in for a tough matchup this week, however, with Baltimore's defense allowing just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to WRs in Week 1.

player.seasonOutlook: Olave is fresh off a career year in which he reached new highs in targets (156), receptions (100), yardage (1,163) and touchdowns (nine). He finished eighth among receivers in fantasy PPG, which beat out his previous career best of 19th in 2023. Olave finished no lower than seventh among receivers in nearly every counting stat, including end zone targets (12) and air yards (1,816). The big season was a sigh of relief after a 2024 campaign riddled with concussions, and it positions the 26-year-old right back in the fringe-WR1 discussion. Especially with No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson expected to miss a month or two with a hamstring injury, Olave will remain Tyler Shough's top target, and that sets him up for another highly productive campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emeka Egbuka is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's top receiver in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns, whose defense struggled against wideouts in Week 1. Despite logging just six targets last week, Egbuka led the Buccaneers in receiving yards, solidifying himself as the team's top WR. Additionally, Egbuka had been nursing a toe injury leading up to the Week 1 loss, so he should only become more explosive as the season progresses. He's in for an incredible Week 2 matchup, as Cleveland's secondary allowed 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts last week, the third-most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Egbuka is a fascinating evaluation following a rookie season that couldn't have started much better (five TDs and 20.5 fantasy PPG during his first five games), but that fell apart from there (one TD and 7.8 PPG during his final 12 games). By season's end, Egbuka sat in the top 10 in targets and air yards, but a horrific 49% catch rate led to a 34th-place finish in fantasy PPG. The good news is that, with Mike Evans out of the picture and Chris Godwin now 30 years old, Egbuka has a shot to emerge as Baker Mayfield's No. 1 target. The 2025 first-round pick is a strong bet for a leap forward and should be viewed as a WR2 with the potential for a full-on breakout.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bhayshul Tuten is likely to get the majority of touches in Jacksonville's backfield in Week 2 against the Broncos, just as he did in the season-opening win over the Browns. Tuten turned 16 touches into 88 yards in Week 1, while Chris Rodriguez and Ameer Abdullah combined for 55 yards on 11 touches, though Rodriguez siphoned some valuable goal-line work. Denver's defense gave up the second-fewest rushing yards in the NFL last season but just allowed Chiefs RBs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson to combine for 259 scrimmage yards and two TDs in a Week 1 loss. Tuten has RB2 upside given his prominent role in a high-powered Jaguars offense, but he's more of a flex/RB3 for Week 2 against a talented Broncos defense searching for a rebound in their home opener.

player.seasonOutlook: Tuten is positioned to take over lead-back duties in Jacksonville following the offseason departure of Travis Etienne Jr. Tuten played sparingly as a rookie, totaling 83 carries and 14 targets in 15 games. He cleared 10 touches in only one game (a 15-touch, 74-yard effort in Week 11), but he did find the end zone in all four games in which he had at least eight touches. The 2025 fourth-round pick will see some scoring regression (seven TDs on 93 touches), but he flashed in limited work, can contribute as a rusher and receiver, is working in a good offense and has only journeyman Chris Rodriguez Jr. and passing-down specialist LeQuint Allen Jr. as his competition. Tuten is still unproven, but the 23-year-old has a path to a breakout season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jadarian Price is set for his second NFL start when Seattle travels to Arizona in Week 2. Price was efficient in his professional debut last Wednesday versus New England, rushing 10 times for 52 yards while catching both of his targets for six yards. George Holani was given eight carries in the win, which helped limit Price's workload. The split between the two going forward remains to be seen, but there's certainly a chance that Price's touches will increase as the season progresses. The Cardinals' run defense looked good against the Chargers in Week 1, holding Omarion Hampton to 43 yards on 12 carries.

player.seasonOutlook: Price was selected by the Seahawks with the No. 32 overall pick of April's draft. Price managed only 280 career carries while stuck behind Jeremiyah Love at Notre Dame, but he showed well, posting a 4.13 YAC (second best in this rookie class) and 3.6 forced missed tackle rate (third best). He wasn't a factor as a receiver, however, totaling 15 receptions in 41 games. Price has a path to an immediate feature role in Seattle's run-first offense, though he may eventually defer substantial work to Zach Charbonnet (ACL recovery). Value Price as a flex, though he should land on the weekly RB2 radar while Charbonnet is sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Williams will look to build off a monster performance as the Bears take on the Vikings at home in Week 2. Williams delivered for Chicago in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The third-year quarterback completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns while carrying the ball 10 times for 65 yards and two more TDs. Williams will have more of a challenge this upcoming Sunday, given that the Vikings allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (14.3) to quarterbacks in the 2025 season. Still, Minnesota's secondary is susceptible, as they ceded 387 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to Jordan Love this past Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams enters his third NFL season after a solid rookie campaign in 2024 followed by a big leap forward in 2025. Williams finished last season no lower than 11th among QBs in pass attempts, completions, pass yards, passing TDs, carries, rush yards, rush TDs and fantasy points per game. While Williams' completion percentage was one of the worst in the league (58%), his dual-threat ability and turnover avoidance (seven INTs both seasons) has led to solid fantasy output. The 2024 No. 1 draft pick has a good supporting cast in playcaller Ben Johnson and a trio of young pass catchers in Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. Williams is a fringe QB1 with upside for another leap.

outlooksByWeek.2: Stefon Diggs had more than double the targets of teammate Terry McLaurin in Week 1 for Washington. Diggs was targeted a team-high nine times, though managed only four catches. However, he gained 55 yards and also found the end zone, though had a costly celebration penalty on the score that cost Washington a chance to go for two and tie the game late. Still, it was an extremely promising start for Diggs, who will have a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus Dallas. The Cowboys allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to the Giants in their season opener.

player.seasonOutlook: Diggs signed with the Commanders in August after he was released by the Patriots earlier this offseason. Successful in his return from an ACL tear suffered midway through 2024, the veteran receiver's lone season in New England resulted in 85 catches (ninth among wide receivers) and his seventh career 1,000-yard campaign. Diggs paced the position with an incredible 83% catch rate (second highest all time for a receiver with 100-plus targets) and ranked fourth in yards per route run (2.8). Not used much near the goal line, however, Diggs was limited to four touchdowns and finished 23rd in fantasy PPG. He obviously still has something left in the tank, but is now 32 years old and his usage is trending downward. He has a path to a substantial offense role in Washington and can be viewed as a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Likely scored twice in his debut for the Giants in Week 1, leading a stunning victory over the Cowboys. Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and the two scores to lead the Giants in receiving. Especially in the red zone and on third down, quarterback Jaxson Dart leaned heavily on his new tight end, something that should continue in Week 2 versus the Rams. Los Angeles allowed 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in its dismal season-opening loss to the 49ers, while also losing star acquisition Myles Garrett to a knee injury. Aaron Donald will make his return from retirement to help out the defensive line, though.

player.seasonOutlook: Likely signed with the Giants after four years of backing up Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Likely is reuniting with coach John Harbaugh and is finally expected to play a consistent offensive role. During his time in Baltimore, Likely was limited to 50% of the team's offensive snaps and never finished a season better than 20th among tight ends in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards or fantasy PPG. His only extensive stretch with Andrews sidelined came back in 2023. During the seven-game span, Likely posted a 23-356-6 receiving line on a 16% target share and averaged a solid 13.5 fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old is obviously unproven, but his receiving skills in New York's ascending offense are enough to put him on the TE2 radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wan'Dale Robinson had at least a share of the team lead in targets, catches, and receiving yards in his Titans debut, though he had a modest five catches for 38 yards on six targets. Tennessee's passing offense may not improve much, if at all, in Week 2 against an Eagles defense that allowed just six touchdowns to wide receivers last season, which tied for the fewest in the NFL. Robinson relies on target volume to make up for a lack of downfield playmaking capabilities, and the Titans may not throw often or effectively enough for him to make much of a fantasy difference. He's a low-end flex option for Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson signed with the Titans after catching 90-plus passes each of the past two seasons. The 2022 second-round pick has progressively improved his production each season in the pros, peaking with a 30% target share (ninth among WRs), 1,014 yards (13th) and 13.6 fantasy PPG (16th) in 2025. An undersized, short-range slot target, Robinson isn't positioned for many big plays and is very rarely used near the goal line (he's yet to clear four TDs in a season and has 13 career end zone targets). In Tennessee, Robinson will battle rookie Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley for the team lead in targets, but his potential for flex production will depend on whether Cam Ward is able to make a Year 2 leap. Robinson, 25, is a low-ceiling, middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: KC Concepcion and the Browns are on the road in Week 2 to face the Buccaneers and their eighth-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed to WRs (101). The rookie looked hungry and fought for more on every play, catching four of five targets for 43 yards and rushing three times for 15 yards while losing a fumble. Concepcion's blunder came on a play from behind as he tried to gain extra yardage, but it was still a promising debut for the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, as he led the team in receptions and targets. Still, it's difficult to trust anyone on the Browns' offense, especially against a Tampa Bay defense that held Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to 71 combined yards.

player.seasonOutlook: Concepcion was selected by the Browns in the first round of April's draft. He is a quick and explosive short-to-intermediate receiver whose career 27.2% target share topped this entire rookie class. Primarily a slot receiver during his first two seasons at NC State, Concepcion played more on the outside in 2025 at Texas A&M, but he figures to primarily work inside in the pros (career 72% slot rate), while also helping as a rusher and returner. Concepcion will need to fend off the likes of Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie Denzel Boston for targets in an offense with quarterback issues, so while he has upside, he's best valued as a flex.

This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Little got off to an accurate start by converting both of his field-goal attempts and all four extra points in Jacksonville's Week 1 win. He made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season, so there are no concerns about his leg strength. Getting into scoring range will be tougher than usual for the Jaguars in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the league last season, though 70 yards could be within Little's realistic range in the thin Denver air. Little's upside is high enough to maintain fantasy starter status, even given the tricky Week 2 matchup for Jacksonville's offense.

Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kaelon Black is coming off an impressive NFL debut as San Francisco heads into a Week 2 matchup versus the Dolphins. Black surprisingly got more carries than Christian McCaffrey in a season-opening win over the Rams, logging 14 carries for 65 yards to McCaffrey's 10 carries for 68 yards. While there's no chance of Black usurping a healthy McCaffrey in the pecking order anytime soon, the Week 1 usage suggests Black could take on a significant role in San Francisco's offense if the team looks to lighten McCaffrey's workload. Both backs could be in for a good day against Miami, who allowed Las Vegas running backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington to combine for 143 rushing yards, 45 receiving yards and two touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.

player.seasonOutlook: Black was selected by the 49ers in the third round of April's draft. It was a bit of a surprise selection after Black failed to clear 190 touches in four collegiate seasons prior to not landing an invite to the scouting combine. He did clear 1,000 rushing yards at Indiana in 2025, but remained a nonfactor as a receiver, totaling exactly four receptions in each of his two seasons with the Hoosiers. Black will open his career handling No. 2 duties behind Christian McCaffrey. He'll be worth an add if the 30-year-old McCaffrey misses time, but a lack of third-down ability may severely limit his fantasy output. Stash Black in dynasty formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep it rolling in Detroit's Week 2 matchup at Buffalo. Gibbs was the bell cow managers hoped for in Week 1 against the Saints, logging 29 rushes for 156 yards, two touchdowns and catching all five of his targets for 30 yards. He'll also face a Bills defense that fared badly against the ground game in their season opener, allowing Gibbs' former teammate David Montgomery to total 79 yards and three touchdowns off 23 touches.

player.seasonOutlook: Gibbs has finished in the top 10 among running backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions, touchdowns and fantasy points in each of his first three campaigns. In fact, his 38 touchdowns over the past two seasons are four more than any other player. Though Gibbs has finished as a top-three fantasy back in each of the past two years, he has yet to finish a season higher than seventh in touches. That very well could change this season with David Montgomery no longer in the mix. The 24-year-old Gibbs is one of the NFL's top playmakers in one of its best offenses. He's a strong option with the first pick of fantasy drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ashton Jeanty looked like a franchise back in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins, turning 29 touches into 147 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The ankle injury that limited him in training camp and the preseason was no longer an issue, and the second-year RB dominated the workload, as rookie backup Mike Washington notched only seven carries. Jeanty's pass-catching role could be cut back once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to return, but he will remain a focal point of the offense heading into a Week 2 clash with a Chargers defense that ranked second in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeanty is eyeing a leap forward in his second NFL season after an uneven rookie campaign in which the first-round pick enjoyed a ton of volume (seventh among backs in carries, targets and receptions) and played fairly well (eighth among RBs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF) but struggled to overcome the shaky Las Vegas offense. The good news is that the Raiders' offense should improve in 2026 with a better/healthier offensive line, a new coach in Super Bowl champion Klint Kubiak and a new quarterback in projected No. 1 NFL draft pick Fernando Mendoza. Jeanty has a clean path to a massive offensive role and is a strong bet for a leap forward. The 22-year-old is a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Nico Collins is in danger of sitting out against the Bengals in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury.
